title: An infrared portrait of the barred spiral galaxy Messier 83
caption: The barred spiral galaxy Messier 83 in infrared light, imaged at ESO's La Silla Observatory
captureDate: May 2001 (Ks and J images) and February 1998 (I image)
captureShort: May 2001 (Ks and J images) and February 1998 (I image)
celestial: M 83, Messier 83, NGC 5236 · constellation Hydra · about 15 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This false-colour infrared photo shows the nearby barred spiral galaxy Messier 83. A barred spiral has a straight band of stars across its centre, from which the spiral arms unwind.

The picture blends three images taken at different infrared wavelengths. Two came from the SOFI instrument on ESO's 3.5-metre New Technology Telescope, and the third from the DFOSC instrument on the Danish 1.54-metre telescope, both at La Silla Observatory in Chile.

The two SOFI images were each built from exposures of four neighbouring fields stitched together into a mosaic. Before combining them, the team subtracted a matching sky frame from every exposure to remove the glow of the sky itself. The third image was reshaped so that its pixels and field of view matched the others, allowing all three to be layered into one picture in which north is up.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (9.02 x 8.75 arcminutes) and distance (15 million light years), the frame spans roughly 39,000 × 38,000 light-years. Its light set out about 15 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This infrared composite combines Ks-band and J-band images from SOFI on the New Technology Telescope with an I-band image from DFOSC on the Danish 1.54-metre telescope. Ks is shown in red, J in green and I in blue.
